text: Ministry proposes up to 85 per cent reduction in penalties to facilitate tax code closures

HÀ NỘI - The Ministry of Finance has proposed administrative fines be reduced by up to 85 per cent for household and individual businesses filing tax declarations as part of efforts to clear backlogs of inactive taxpayer codes and simplify procedures for businesses seeking to close their tax accounts.
The ministry made the proposal in the latest draft version of a Government resolution it submitted following revisions based on recent feedback.

Under the draft, household and individual business operators paying tax through the declaration method would face fines equivalent to just 15 per cent of the normal penalties for late tax returns and violations involving the preparation and submission of invoice notifications and reports.
This represents a reduction of 85 per cent, compared with the initial proposed cut of 50 per cent.
To qualify, affected businesses must submit all outstanding tax declarations and required invoice notifications and reports.
The proposed preferential rate would apply from November 21, 2026 to June 30, 2028.
Household businesses and individual operators paying tax under the presumptive method would be exempt from administrative penalties for tax procedure violations covered by the resolution.
For other taxpayers, including companies, the draft sets out a phased penalty reduction based on when outstanding documents are completed.
Those submitting all outstanding documents between November 21, 2026, and June 30, 2027 would pay 30 per cent of the standard fines, equivalent to a 70 per cent reduction.
This rate would rise to 50 per cent of the normal penalty for submissions made between July 1 and December 31, 2027, and 70 per cent for those completed between January 1 and June 30, 2028.
The ministry said the phased approach was designed to encourage taxpayers to address outstanding obligations as early as possible.
The special measures would not apply to tax evasion or fraud, or taxpayers under inspection, audit, investigation, prosecution or trial for such violations.
Alongside lower penalties, the draft proposes exemptions from certain tax declarations and invoice reports for taxpayers who had no tax obligations during the relevant periods.

Eligible taxpayers would not be required to submit tax declarations for periods in which no tax liabilities arose, starting from the time they were identified as no longer operating at their registered addresses or from the date their business registration certificates were revoked, as applicable.
They would also be exempt from preparing and submitting invoice reports for periods before July 1, 2022, if they had not actually used invoices during those periods.

The draft also authorises tax authorities to terminate the tax codes of taxpayers that have ceased operations or have not operated at their registered addresses for at least 10 consecutive years as of June 30, 2028.

This would be conditional on taxpayers having no outstanding tax debts at the time of termination, not being subject to investigations or legal proceedings over tax or invoice violations, and having no unresolved indications of tax evasion or fraud.
Before terminating the tax codes, tax authorities would have to publicly announce the proposed list for 30 days.
If no applications for restoration or written objections from relevant parties were received within that period, the authorities could proceed with the termination.
The draft also includes a safeguard for individuals whose identities have been misused to establish companies or household businesses.
It is expected to take effect on November 21, with the special support measures remaining in force until June 30, 2028, except for certain cases handled under transitional provisions.
The Ministry of Finance previously cited the case of a company that had ceased operations for 10 years without conducting any production or business activities.

In this case, the company could be required to submit 50 outstanding tax documents to complete the termination of its tax codes, including 40 value-added tax declarations and 10 corporate income tax finalisation returns.

It could also face financial obligations of approximately VNĐ55 million (US$2,100), including VNĐ23 million in penalties for late tax filings, VNĐ20 million in business licence fees and VNĐ12 million in late-payment interest on those fees.

The ministry said accumulated administrative penalties over several years had become a major obstacle for inactive taxpayers seeking to complete procedures to restore or terminate their tax identification numbers.
The proposed resolution aims to address these difficulties while ensuring that taxpayers still fulfil their underlying tax obligations. - VNS
